name: Ndolé
subtitle: Ndolé is a Cameroonian dish of bitter leaves (Vernonia, also called bitterleaf) cooked with groundnut paste, to which meat, smoked fish or shrimp are added.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A Cameroonian dish made from ndolé leaves and groundnut paste.

facts.label: Main ingredient
facts.value: The leaves are Vernonia, known as ndolé or bitterleaf, one of the most widely eaten leafy vegetables in Cameroon.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: The green leaves are boiled in water two or three times with rock salt to remove their bitterness.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: In local processing, raw or boiled leaves are squeezed and washed to remove the bitter taste and foam.

facts.label: Other ingredients
facts.value: Shrimp, smoked fish, smoked meat or vegetables may be added to the leaves and groundnut paste.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: An old dish of the Sawa people that quickly became a national dish.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: The leaves are washed, beaten and rinsed several times to tame the bitterness, then combined with groundnut paste, spices and a protein: meat, smoked fish or shrimp.

facts.label: Neighbouring versions
facts.value: The leaf dish is also known in Benin (Amanvivè) and Togo (Aloma), but only Cameroon combines it with meat, shellfish and groundnut.

facts.label: Versions and social meaning
facts.value: Versions range from simple (meat), to mixed (meat and smoked fish), to 'royal' (meat, smoked fish and shrimp), which indicate the family's social category.

facts.label: How it is eaten
facts.value: Served with plantain (fried or boiled), cassava or rice.

facts.label: Who makes it
facts.value: The recipe is passed down through the generations, most often between women, and there are almost as many versions as families.

facts.label: Date
facts.value: 'Ndolè Sawa' was registered as a collective trademark with OAPI for 10 years; the certificate was handed to the president of the Ngondo on 27 October 2026.

parts.text: Ndolé is a Cameroonian dish of bitter leaves (Vernonia, also called bitterleaf) cooked with groundnut paste, to which meat, smoked fish or shrimp are added. The leaves are boiled two or three times, or washed and squeezed, to remove their bitterness. It is an old dish of the Sawa people of the Littoral that became a national dish, and in October 2026 the name 'Ndolè Sawa' was registered as a collective trademark with the African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI).
It is eaten with plantain (fried or boiled), cassava or rice. Its versions range from meat only to meat with smoked fish and shrimp, which signals a family's social standing.
